capabilities: Toggle properties visibility with a ribbon click or bound hotkey
Temporarily peek at hidden properties for 2-60 seconds on a timer
Explicitly hide or show properties via commands
Configure startup behaviour, peek duration, source-mode hiding, and per-device state
disambiguation: Not a properties or frontmatter editor; it only changes whether the frontmatter block is visible and never modifies note files.
extras: Install is via GitHub Releases only (no community plugin store listing mentioned). The README includes compatibility notes for heavily customised themes overriding .metadata-container, and states the Properties side-panel stays visible while in-note properties are hidden.
intentEvidence: Obsidian's built-in setting (Settings → Editor → Properties in document → Hidden) can hide properties, but it comes with everyday friction
motivation: The README's 'Why Properties Peek?' section explains the author wanted to remove the everyday friction of the built-in hidden setting (no ribbon toggle, no hotkey, no temporary peek).
problem: Obsidian's built-in 'Properties in document: Hidden' setting has no quick toggle, hotkey, or way to glance at properties briefly, so users must dig through settings each time.
summary: Property visibility toggle that hides or shows the YAML frontmatter block across open notes, with a timed temporary peek.
